title: ECTODERMAL DYSPLASIA 17 WITH OR WITHOUT LIMB MALFORMATIONS

relationships.phenotype: ECTODERMAL DYSPLASIA 17 WITH OR WITHOUT LIMB MALFORMATIONS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that ectodermal dysplasia-17 with or without limb malformations (ECTD17) is caused by heterozygous or homozygous mutation in the LEF1 gene on chromosome 4q25.

checks.claim: Ectodermal dysplasia-17 with or without limb malformations (ECTD17) is caused by heterozygous or homozygous mutation in the LEF1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Our findings establish mono- and biallelic variants in LEF1 as a cause for a novel syndrome comprising limb malformations and ectodermal dysplasia.
checks.explanation: Monoallelic (heterozygous) and biallelic variants (in a consanguineous family, so presumably homozygous) are said to cause the syndrome. The name ECTD17 is OMIM's label for it.

checks.claim: The LEF1 gene is located on chromosome 4q25.
checks.evidence_quote: We report two unrelated patients with 4q25 de novo deletion encompassing LEF1
checks.explanation: The abstract places LEF1 within a 4q25 deletion.

paragraphs.text: Ectodermal dysplasia-17 with or without limb malformations (ECTD17) is a disorder caused by variants in LEF1, which encodes a transcription factor acting downstream of the WNT-beta-catenin signaling pathway. Features include hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia with severe oligodontia, hypotrichosis, and hypohidrosis. Some patients also have limb malformations, such as radial ray defects, polydactyly, or split hand/foot (Lévy et al., 2020; Dufour et al., 2022).

checks.claim: ECTD17 is a disorder caused by variants in LEF1.
checks.evidence_quote: We provide further evidence for LEF1 haploinsufficiency role in ectodermal dysplasia and delineate its clinical phenotype.
checks.explanation: The abstract links LEF1 haploinsufficiency to ectodermal dysplasia.

checks.claim: LEF1 encodes a transcription factor acting downstream of the WNT-beta-catenin signaling pathway.
checks.evidence_quote: Wnt/β-catenin pathway requires the lymphoid enhancer-binding factor 1 (LEF1), a nuclear mediator, to activate target gene expression.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes LEF1 as a nuclear mediator that activates target genes in the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, which matches the claim.

paragraphs.text: Dufour et al. (2022) reported 12 individuals with LEF1 variants. Eleven were from 4 unrelated families, and 1 was from a consanguineous family. The phenotypic spectrum included ectodermal dysplasia and various limb malformations, such as radial ray defects, polydactyly, or split hand/foot.

paragraphs.text: The de novo occurrence of the deletions including LEF1 in the patients reported by Lévy et al. (2020) indicated autosomal dominant inheritance through haploinsufficiency. Dufour et al. (2022) stated that, depending on the type and location of the LEF1 variant, the disorder can be inherited in either an autosomal dominant or an autosomal recessive manner.

checks.evidence_quote: We provide further evidence for LEF1 haploinsufficiency role in ectodermal dysplasia
checks.explanation: The abstract reports de novo deletions and haploinsufficiency, but it does not explicitly state autosomal dominant inheritance. That is an inference.

paragraphs.text: Lévy et al. (2020) identified de novo deletions at chromosome 4q25 that included the LEF1 gene in 2 unrelated patients with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia. They concluded that the findings provided further evidence that LEF1 haploinsufficiency causes ectodermal dysplasia. They noted that no pathogenic variants involving LEF1 had previously been reported in humans.

checks.evidence_quote: We report two unrelated patients with 4q25 de novo deletion encompassing LEF1, associated with severe oligodontia of primary and permanent dentition, hypotrichosis and hypohidrosis compatible with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia.
checks.explanation: The abstract matches this claim.

paragraphs.text: Using high-throughput sequencing, Dufour et al. (2022) identified monoallelic LEF1 variants in 11 affected individuals from 4 unrelated families. They also identified a biallelic LEF1 variant in an affected individual from a consanguineous family. The authors noted that LEF1 had earlier been suspected as a candidate gene for ectodermal dysplasia in 2 individuals with chromosome 4q microdeletions. Their functional studies used immunofluorescence, immunoblotting, pulldown assays, and RNA sequencing. Transcriptomic studies showed altered WNT signaling associated with the LEF1 variants.

checks.evidence_quote: High-throughput sequencing was employed to delineate the genetic underpinnings of the disease.
checks.explanation: The abstract names high-throughput sequencing as the method.

checks.explanation: This matches the abstract.

checks.explanation: The abstract specifies 4q35 microdeletions, so the draft's '4q microdeletions' is a less specific but consistent restatement.

checks.explanation: The same methods are listed. The abstract says 'and/or', so not every method may have been applied to every variant.

checks.explanation: The abstract states that transcriptomic studies showed altered WNT signaling.

paragraphs.text: From their functional studies, Dufour et al. (2022) proposed 2 molecular mechanisms. Haploinsufficiency or loss of DNA binding was responsible for a mild to moderate phenotype. In contrast, loss of beta-catenin binding caused by biallelic variants was associated with a severe phenotype.

checks.explanation: The abstract proposes 2 mechanisms based on functional data.

checks.evidence_quote: haploinsufficiency or loss of DNA binding are responsible for a mild to moderate phenotype
checks.explanation: This matches the abstract.

checks.claim: Dufour et al. (2022) proposed that loss of beta-catenin binding caused by biallelic LEF1 variants was associated with a severe phenotype.

checks.explanation: This matches the abstract.
